topics.title: Why study geography and what geography is

concepts.learning_objective: State the origin and meaning of the term geography and who coined it.
Distinguish physical features of the earth's surface from cultural features created by human beings.

topics.title: Areal differentiation, causal relationships and nature-human interaction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain geography as the study of areal differentiation and of the causes behind spatial variation.
Explain how human beings adapt to and modify nature, producing humanised nature and naturalised humans.

topics.title: The three questions of geography and spatial organisation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the what, where and why questions and explain why the why question made geography scientific.
Explain how links (routes) and nodes (settlements) organise and integrate space.
Explain geography as a discipline of spatial synthesis compared with history's temporal synthesis.
Analyse how geographical factors such as distance, mountains and seas have shaped historical events.
Explain how time and space can be converted into each other and why time is the fourth dimension.

topics.title: Branches of geography: approaches and sub-fields

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the systematic approach of Humboldt from the regional approach of Ritter.
Classify sub-fields such as geomorphology, climatology, hydrology and political geography into physical, human and biogeography.
Identify the branches based on the regional approach and the philosophy and methods common to all branches.
Identify the four realms studied in physical geography and what each includes.
Evaluate the importance of physical geography for resource management and sustainable development.
